newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Moscow ready for long-term deal with rebel Chechnya.
newsitem.headline: Moscow ready for long-term deal with rebel Chechnya.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin said on Monday he was ready to negotiate a long-term political deal with Chechnya but made clear he still viewed the rebel region as an integral part of Russia, Russian news agencies said.
"We will solve the problems as we did with Shaimiyev," Interfax quoted him as saying after talks with Chechen President Aslan Maskhadov.
He was referring to the wide-reaching autonomy granted in 1994 to Tatarstan, a republic on the Volga River in the Russian interior, and its regional leader Mintimer Shaimiyev.

"We should without stubborness continue steps towards the freedom of the Chechen Republic," RIA news agency quoted Yeltsin as saying after 90 minutes of talks in the Kremlin. "I am ready for such steps."
Itar-Tass news agency quoted Maskhadov as saying the agreement should be finalised soon.
Yeltsin said a joint working group would be set up to hammer out the details of the agreement, according to Interfax.
Chechen and Russian representatives were due to brief reporters later on the talks between the two presidents.

Russia and Chechnya ended 20 months of war with a peace deal last August under which Moscow withdrew its troops from the rebel region in exchange for the separatists' promise not to raise the issue of the region's future status until 2001.
Maskhadov had said before the talks that he wanted full independence for his region. Moscow has ruled out granting independence to Chechnya, offering strong autonomy instead.
